title: The most important lesson from 83,000 brain scans | Daniel Amen | TEDxOrangeCoast

blocks.en_text: In this talk, I'm going to give you the single most important lesson
blocks.zh_text: 在这次演讲中，我要告诉你们最重要的一课

blocks.en_text: my colleagues and I have learned from looking at 83,000 brain scans.
blocks.zh_text: 这是我和同事们从八万三千份脑部扫描中学到的。

blocks.en_text: But first, let me put the lesson into context.
blocks.zh_text: 但首先，让我先讲讲这一课的背景。

blocks.en_text: I am in the middle of seven children.
blocks.zh_text: 我在家里七个孩子中排行中间。

blocks.en_text: Growing up, my father called me a maverick
blocks.zh_text: 从小到大，我父亲都叫我“独行侠”

blocks.en_text: which to him was not a good thing.
blocks.zh_text: 在他眼里，这可不是什么好事。

blocks.en_text: In 1972, the army called my number,
blocks.zh_text: 1972年，军队征召了我，

blocks.en_text: and I was trained as an infantry medic where my love of medicine was born.
blocks.zh_text: 我被训练成一名步兵卫生员，我对医学的热爱就是从那时开始的。

blocks.en_text: But since I truly hated the idea of being shot at or sleeping in the mud,
blocks.zh_text: 但因为我是真的讨厌被人开枪打、讨厌睡在泥地里，

blocks.en_text: I got myself retrained as an X-ray technician
blocks.zh_text: 我就让自己重新受训，成了一名X光技师，

blocks.en_text: and developed a passion for medical imaging.
blocks.zh_text: 并对医学影像产生了浓厚的兴趣。

blocks.en_text: As our professors used to say: "How do you know, unless you look?"
blocks.zh_text: 就像我们的教授常说的：“你不去看，怎么会知道？”

blocks.en_text: In 1979, when I was a second-year medical student,
blocks.zh_text: 1979年，我还是个二年级的医学生，

blocks.en_text: someone in my family became seriously suicidal,
blocks.zh_text: 我家里有人出现了严重的自杀倾向，

blocks.en_text: and I took her to see a wonderful psychiatrist.
blocks.zh_text: 我带她去看了一位很棒的精神科医生。

blocks.en_text: Over time, I realized if he helped her, which he did,
blocks.zh_text: 随着时间推移，我意识到，如果他帮到了她——而他确实帮到了——

blocks.en_text: it would not only save her life,
blocks.zh_text: 那不仅会救她的命，

blocks.en_text: but it would also help her children and even her future grandchildren,
blocks.zh_text: 还会帮到她的孩子，甚至她未来的孙辈，

blocks.en_text: as they would be shaped by someone who is happier and more stable.
blocks.zh_text: 因为他们会被一个更快乐、更稳定的人所影响。

blocks.en_text: I fell in love with psychiatry
blocks.zh_text: 我爱上了精神医学，

blocks.en_text: because I realized it had the potential to change generations of people.
blocks.zh_text: 因为我意识到它有改变几代人的潜力。

blocks.en_text: In 1991, I went to my first lecture on brain SPECT imaging.
blocks.zh_text: 1991年，我去听了我的第一堂关于脑部SPECT成像的讲座。

blocks.en_text: SPECT is a nuclear medicine study that looks at the blood flow and activity,
blocks.zh_text: SPECT是一种核医学检查，用来观察血流和活动，

blocks.en_text: it looks at how your brain works.
blocks.zh_text: 它看的是你的大脑是如何运作的。

blocks.en_text: SPECT was presented as a tool to help psychiatrists
blocks.zh_text: 当时SPECT被介绍为一种工具，帮助精神科医生

blocks.en_text: get more information to help their patients.
blocks.zh_text: 获取更多信息来帮助他们的病人。

blocks.en_text: In that one lecture, my two professional loves,
blocks.zh_text: 就在那一堂讲座上，我职业上的两大热爱——

blocks.en_text: medical imaging and psychiatry,
blocks.zh_text: 医学影像和精神医学——

blocks.en_text: came together, and quite honestly, revolutionized my life.
blocks.zh_text: 结合在了一起，说实话，这彻底改变了我的生活。

blocks.en_text: Over the next 22 years, my colleagues and I would build
blocks.zh_text: 在接下来的22年里，我和同事们建立了

blocks.en_text: the world's largest database of brain scans related to behavior
blocks.zh_text: 世界上最大的、与行为相关的脑部扫描数据库，

blocks.en_text: on patients from 93 countries.
blocks.zh_text: 病人来自93个国家。

blocks.en_text: SPECT basically tells us three things about the brain:
blocks.zh_text: SPECT基本上能告诉我们关于大脑的三件事：

blocks.en_text: good activity, too little, or too much.
blocks.zh_text: 活动良好、活动太少，或者活动太多。

blocks.en_text: Here's a set of healthy SPECT scans.
blocks.zh_text: 这是一组健康的SPECT扫描图。

blocks.en_text: The image on the left shows the outside surface of the brain,
blocks.zh_text: 左边的图像显示的是大脑的外表面，

blocks.en_text: and a healthy scan shows full, even, symmetrical activity.
blocks.zh_text: 健康的扫描图显示出饱满、均匀、对称的活动。

blocks.en_text: The color is not important, it's the shape that matters.
blocks.zh_text: 颜色不重要，重要的是形状。

blocks.en_text: In the image on the right, red equals the areas of high activity,
blocks.zh_text: 在右边的图像中，红色代表高活动区域，

blocks.en_text: and in a healthy brain, they're typically in the back part of the brain.
blocks.zh_text: 而在健康的大脑中，它们通常位于大脑的后部。

blocks.en_text: Here's a healthy scan compared to someone who had two strokes.
blocks.zh_text: 这是一张健康扫描图，对比一个得过两次中风的人。

blocks.en_text: You can see the holes of activity.
blocks.zh_text: 你能看到那些活动缺失的空洞。

blocks.en_text: Here's what Alzheimer's looks like,
blocks.zh_text: 这是阿尔茨海默病的样子，

blocks.en_text: where the back half of the brain is deteriorating.
blocks.zh_text: 大脑的后半部分在退化。

blocks.en_text: Did you know that Alzheimer's disease actually starts in the brain
blocks.zh_text: 你知道吗，阿尔茨海默病其实在你出现任何症状之前

blocks.en_text: 30 to 50 years before you have any symptoms?
blocks.zh_text: 30到50年就已经在大脑里开始了？

blocks.en_text: Here's a scan of a traumatic brain injury.
blocks.zh_text: 这是一张创伤性脑损伤的扫描图。

blocks.en_text: Your brain is soft, and your skull is really hard.
blocks.zh_text: 你的大脑很软，而你的头骨非常硬。

blocks.en_text: Or drug abuse.
blocks.zh_text: 或者药物滥用。

blocks.en_text: The real reason not to use drugs - they damage your brain.
blocks.zh_text: 不要吸毒的真正原因——它们会损害你的大脑。

blocks.en_text: Obsessive–compulsive disorder
blocks.zh_text: 强迫症

blocks.en_text: where the front part of the brain typically works too hard,
blocks.zh_text: 这种情况下大脑前部通常过度活跃，

blocks.en_text: so that people cannot turn off their thoughts.
blocks.zh_text: 以至于人们无法关掉自己的念头。

blocks.en_text: An epilepsy where we frequently see areas of increased activity.
blocks.zh_text: 还有癫痫，我们经常能看到活动增强的区域。

blocks.en_text: In 1992, I went to an all-day conference on brain SPECT imaging,
blocks.zh_text: 1992年，我去参加了一个为期一整天的脑SPECT成像会议，

blocks.en_text: it was amazing and mirrored
blocks.zh_text: 那太棒了，而且和

blocks.en_text: our own early experience using SPECT in psychiatry.
blocks.zh_text: 我们自己在精神科使用SPECT的早期经验如出一辙。

blocks.en_text: But at that same meeting, researchers started to complain loudly
blocks.zh_text: 但在同一次会议上，研究人员开始大声抱怨

blocks.en_text: that clinical psychiatrists like me should not be doing scans,
blocks.zh_text: 说像我这样的临床精神科医生不该做扫描，

blocks.en_text: that they were only for their research.
blocks.zh_text: 说扫描只供他们做研究用。

blocks.en_text: Being the maverick and having clinical experience,
blocks.zh_text: 作为一个特立独行又有临床经验的人，

blocks.en_text: I thought that was a really dumb idea.
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得那真是个愚蠢的想法。

blocks.en_text: Without imaging,
blocks.zh_text: 没有成像技术，

blocks.en_text: psychiatrists then and even now make diagnosis like they did in 1840,
blocks.zh_text: 精神科医生当时乃至现在做诊断的方式，和1840年一样，

blocks.en_text: when Abraham Lincoln was depressed,
blocks.zh_text: 那时候亚伯拉罕·林肯正患有抑郁症，

blocks.en_text: by talking to people and looking for symptom clusters.
blocks.zh_text: 就是靠和人交谈、寻找症状群来诊断。

blocks.en_text: Imaging was showing us there was a better way.
blocks.zh_text: 成像技术向我们表明，有更好的办法。

blocks.en_text: Did you know that psychiatrists are the only medical specialists
blocks.zh_text: 你知道吗，精神科医生是唯一一种

blocks.en_text: that virtually never look at the organ they treat?
blocks.zh_text: 几乎从不看自己所治疗器官的医学专科医生？

blocks.en_text: Think about it!
blocks.zh_text: 想想看！

blocks.en_text: Cardiologists look, neurologists look, orthopedic doctors look,
blocks.zh_text: 心脏科医生会看，神经科医生会看，骨科医生会看，

blocks.en_text: virtually every other medical specialties look -
blocks.zh_text: 几乎其他所有医学专科都会看——

blocks.en_text: psychiatrists guess.
blocks.zh_text: 而精神科医生靠猜。

blocks.en_text: Before imaging,
blocks.zh_text: 在有了成像技术之前，

blocks.en_text: I always felt like I was throwing darts in the dark at my patients
blocks.zh_text: 我总觉得自己像是在黑暗中朝病人扔飞镖

blocks.en_text: and had hurt some of them which horrified me.
blocks.zh_text: 还伤到了其中一些人，这让我惊恐不已。

blocks.en_text: There is a reason
blocks.zh_text: 这是有原因的，

blocks.en_text: that most psychiatric medications have black box warnings.
blocks.zh_text: 大多数精神科药物都带有黑框警告。

blocks.en_text: Give them to the wrong person, and you can precipitate a disaster.
blocks.zh_text: 把它们给错了人，就可能引发一场灾难。

blocks.en_text: Early on, our imaging work taught us many important lessons,
blocks.zh_text: 早期，我们的成像工作教会了我们许多重要的经验，

blocks.en_text: such as illnesses, like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and addictions,
blocks.zh_text: 比如像多动症、焦虑、抑郁和成瘾这类疾病，

blocks.en_text: are not simple or single disorders in the brain,
blocks.zh_text: 在大脑里并不是简单或单一的障碍，

blocks.en_text: they all have multiple types.
blocks.zh_text: 它们都有多种类型。

blocks.en_text: For example, here are two patients
blocks.zh_text: 举个例子，这是两位病人，

blocks.en_text: who have been diagnosed with major depression,
blocks.zh_text: 他们都被诊断患有重度抑郁症，

blocks.en_text: that had virtually the same symptoms, yet radically different brains.
blocks.zh_text: 症状几乎完全相同，大脑却截然不同。

blocks.en_text: One had really low activity in the brain, the other one had really high activity.
blocks.zh_text: 一个人的大脑活动非常低，另一个人的大脑活动非常高。

blocks.en_text: How would you ever know what to do for them, unless you actually looked?
blocks.zh_text: 除非你真的去看一看，否则你怎么可能知道该怎么帮他们？

blocks.en_text: Treatment needs to be tailored
blocks.zh_text: 治疗需要量身定制

blocks.en_text: to individual brains, not clusters of symptoms.
blocks.zh_text: 针对每个个体的大脑，而不是针对一堆症状。

blocks.en_text: Our imaging work also taught us
blocks.zh_text: 我们的影像工作还让我们认识到

blocks.en_text: that mild traumatic brain injury was a major cause of psychiatric illness
blocks.zh_text: 轻度创伤性脑损伤是精神疾病的一个主要原因

blocks.en_text: that ruin people's lives,
blocks.zh_text: 这些疾病会毁掉人们的生活，

blocks.en_text: and virtually no one knew about it because they would see psychiatrists
blocks.zh_text: 而几乎没有人知道这一点，因为他们会去看精神科医生

blocks.en_text: for things like temper problems, anxiety, depression, and insomnia,
blocks.zh_text: 看的是脾气问题、焦虑、抑郁和失眠这类毛病，

blocks.en_text: and they would never look, so they would never know.
blocks.zh_text: 而医生从来不会去查看，所以他们永远不会知道。

blocks.en_text: Here's a scan of a 15-year-old boy
blocks.zh_text: 这是一张15岁男孩的扫描图

blocks.en_text: who felt down a flight of stairs at the age of three.
blocks.zh_text: 他三岁时从一段楼梯上摔了下来。

blocks.en_text: Even though he was unconscious for only a few minutes,
blocks.zh_text: 尽管他只昏迷了几分钟，

blocks.en_text: there was nothing mild about the enduring effect
blocks.zh_text: 但那次受伤对他人生造成的持久影响

blocks.en_text: that injury had on this boy's life.
blocks.zh_text: 一点也不轻微。

blocks.en_text: When I met him at the age of 15, he had just been kicked out
blocks.zh_text: 我15岁见到他时，他刚刚被赶出

blocks.en_text: of his third residential treatment program for violence.
blocks.zh_text: 他的第三个寄宿式治疗项目，原因是暴力行为。

blocks.en_text: He needed a brain rehabilitation program,
blocks.zh_text: 他需要的是一个大脑康复项目，

blocks.en_text: not just more medication thrown at him in the dark,
blocks.zh_text: 而不是在黑暗中给他灌更多药，

blocks.en_text: or behavioral therapy which, if you think about it, is really cruel.
blocks.zh_text: 也不是行为疗法——你想想就知道，那其实很残忍。

blocks.en_text: To put him on a behavioral therapy program
blocks.zh_text: 让他去做行为疗法，

blocks.en_text: when behavior is really an expression of the problem, it's not the problem.
blocks.zh_text: 可行为其实只是问题的表现，它并不是问题本身。

blocks.en_text: Researchers have found that undiagnosed brain injuries
blocks.zh_text: 研究人员发现，未被诊断出的脑损伤

blocks.en_text: are a major cause of homelessness, drug and alcohol abuse, depression,
blocks.zh_text: 是无家可归、吸毒酗酒、抑郁、

blocks.en_text: panic attacks, ADHD, and suicide.
blocks.zh_text: 惊恐发作、多动症和自杀的一个主要原因。

blocks.en_text: We are in for a pending disaster
blocks.zh_text: 我们正面临一场即将到来的灾难

blocks.en_text: with the hundreds and thousands of soldiers
blocks.zh_text: 随着成百上千的士兵

blocks.en_text: coming back from Iraq and Afganistan,
blocks.zh_text: 从伊拉克和阿富汗返回，

blocks.en_text: and virtually no one is looking at the function of their brain.
blocks.zh_text: 而几乎没人在检查他们的大脑功能。

blocks.en_text: As we continued our work with SPECT,
blocks.zh_text: 随着我们继续用SPECT开展工作，

blocks.en_text: the criticism grew louder, but so did the lessons.
blocks.zh_text: 批评声越来越大，但学到的经验也越来越多。

blocks.en_text: Judges and defense attorneys sought our help to understand criminal behavior.
blocks.zh_text: 法官和辩护律师寻求我们的帮助，以理解犯罪行为。

blocks.en_text: Today, we have scanned over 500 convicted felons
blocks.zh_text: 如今，我们已经扫描了500多名被定罪的罪犯

blocks.en_text: including 90 murderers.
blocks.zh_text: 其中包括90名杀人犯。

blocks.en_text: Our work taught us that people who do bad things
blocks.zh_text: 我们的工作让我们认识到，做坏事的人

blocks.en_text: often have troubled brains.
blocks.zh_text: 往往有着出问题的大脑。

blocks.en_text: That was not a surprise.
blocks.zh_text: 这并不令人意外。

blocks.en_text: But what did surprise us
blocks.zh_text: 但让我们意外的是

blocks.en_text: was that many of these brains could be rehabilitated.
blocks.zh_text: 这些大脑中有很多是可以康复的。

blocks.en_text: So here's a radical idea.
blocks.zh_text: 所以这里有一个大胆的想法。

blocks.en_text: What if we evaluated and treated troubled brains
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们去评估并治疗这些有问题的大脑，

blocks.en_text: rather than simply warehousing them in toxic, stressful environments?
blocks.zh_text: 而不是简单地把他们关在有毒、高压的环境里，会怎样？

blocks.en_text: In my experience, we could save tremendous amounts of money
blocks.zh_text: 根据我的经验，我们可以省下巨额资金

blocks.en_text: by making these people more functional,
blocks.zh_text: 让这些人变得更有能力，

blocks.en_text: so when they left prison, they could work,
blocks.zh_text: 这样他们出狱后就能工作，

blocks.en_text: support their families and pay taxes.
blocks.zh_text: 养家糊口，还能交税。

blocks.en_text: Dostoyevsky once said: "A society should be judged
blocks.zh_text: 陀思妥耶夫斯基曾说过：“评判一个社会，

blocks.en_text: not by how well it treats its outstanding citizens,
blocks.zh_text: 不是看它如何对待优秀的公民，

blocks.en_text: but by how it treats its criminals."
blocks.zh_text: 而是看它如何对待罪犯。”

blocks.en_text: Instead of just crime and punishment,
blocks.zh_text: 与其只讲犯罪和惩罚，

blocks.en_text: we should be thinking about crime evaluation and treatment.
blocks.zh_text: 我们应该考虑的是犯罪评估和治疗。

blocks.en_text: So after 22 years and 83,000 scans,
blocks.zh_text: 所以，经过22年和83000次扫描之后，

blocks.en_text: the single most important lesson my colleagues and I have learned
blocks.zh_text: 我和同事们学到的最重要的一课

blocks.en_text: is that you can literally change people's brains.
blocks.zh_text: 就是，你真的可以改变人的大脑。

blocks.en_text: And when you do, you change their life.
blocks.zh_text: 而当你这么做时，你就改变了他们的人生。

blocks.en_text: You are not stuck with the brain you have,
blocks.zh_text: 你不会被现有的大脑困住，

blocks.en_text: you can make it better, and we can prove it.
blocks.zh_text: 你可以让它变得更好，而且我们能证明这一点。

blocks.en_text: My colleagues and I performed the first and largest study
blocks.zh_text: 我和同事们做了第一项也是规模最大的一项研究，

blocks.en_text: on active and retired NFL players,
blocks.zh_text: 研究对象是在役和退役的NFL球员，

blocks.en_text: showing high levels of damage in these players at the time
blocks.zh_text: 结果显示这些球员当时存在高水平的损伤，

blocks.en_text: when the NFL said they didn't know
blocks.zh_text: 而当时NFL说他们不知道

blocks.en_text: if playing football caused long-term brain damage.
blocks.zh_text: 打橄榄球是否会造成长期的大脑损伤。

blocks.en_text: The fact was they didn't want to know.
blocks.zh_text: 事实是他们不想知道。

blocks.en_text: That was not a surprise.
blocks.zh_text: 这并不令人意外。

blocks.en_text: I think, if you get the most thoughtful 9-year-olds together,
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得，如果你把最有想法的9岁孩子聚在一起，

blocks.en_text: and you talk about the brain is soft, about the consistency of soft butter,
blocks.zh_text: 跟他们讲大脑很软，质地像软黄油一样，

blocks.en_text: it's housed in a really hard skull that has many sharp, bony ridges,
blocks.zh_text: 它装在一个非常坚硬的颅骨里，颅骨上有很多尖锐的骨嵴，

blocks.en_text: you know, 28 out of 30 nine-year-olds would go:
blocks.zh_text: 你知道，30个九岁孩子里会有28个说：

blocks.en_text: "Probably a bad idea for your life."
blocks.zh_text: “这对你的人生来说可能不是个好主意。”

blocks.en_text: But what really got us excited was the second part of the study
blocks.zh_text: 但真正让我们兴奋的是研究的第二部分，

blocks.en_text: where we put players on a brain-smart program
blocks.zh_text: 我们让球员参加一个健脑计划，

blocks.en_text: and demonstrated that 80% of them could improve
blocks.zh_text: 并证明其中80%的人可以得到改善，

blocks.en_text: in the areas of blood flow, memory, and mood,
blocks.zh_text: 在血流、记忆和情绪方面，

blocks.en_text: that you are not stuck with the brain you have,
blocks.zh_text: 你不会被现有的大脑困住，

blocks.en_text: you can make it better on a brain-smart program.
blocks.zh_text: 通过健脑计划你可以让它变得更好。

blocks.en_text: How exciting is that?
blocks.zh_text: 这多令人兴奋啊？

blocks.en_text: I am so excited.
blocks.zh_text: 我太激动了。

blocks.en_text: Reversing brain damage is a very exciting new frontier,
blocks.zh_text: 逆转大脑损伤是一个非常令人兴奋的新前沿，

blocks.en_text: but the implications are really much wider.
blocks.zh_text: 但它的意义其实要广泛得多。

blocks.en_text: Here is this scan of a teenage girl who has ADHD,
blocks.zh_text: 这是一张患有ADHD的少女的扫描图，

blocks.en_text: who was cutting herself, failing in school, and fighting with her parents.
blocks.zh_text: 她当时在自残，学业不及格，还和父母吵架。

blocks.en_text: When we improved her brain,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们改善了她的大脑后，

blocks.en_text: she went from D's and F's to A's and B's,
blocks.zh_text: 她的成绩从D和F变成了A和B，

blocks.en_text: and was much more emotionally stable.
blocks.zh_text: 情绪也稳定多了。

blocks.en_text: Here is the scan of Nancy.
blocks.zh_text: 这是Nancy的扫描图。

blocks.en_text: Nancy had been diagnosed with dementia,
blocks.zh_text: Nancy被诊断出患有痴呆症，

blocks.en_text: and her doctor told her husband that he should find a home for her
blocks.zh_text: 她的医生告诉她丈夫，他应该给她找个养老院，

blocks.en_text: because within a year, she would not know his name.
blocks.zh_text: 因为一年之内，她就不会认得他的名字了。

blocks.en_text: But on an intensive, brain-rehabilitation program,
blocks.zh_text: 但在一个密集的大脑康复项目中，

blocks.en_text: Nancy's brain was better, as was her memory,
blocks.zh_text: Nancy的大脑好转了，她的记忆力也一样，

blocks.en_text: and four years later, Nancy still knows her husband's name.
blocks.zh_text: 四年后，Nancy仍然记得她丈夫的名字。

blocks.en_text: Or my favorite story to illustrate this point: Andrew,
blocks.zh_text: 或者用我最喜欢的故事来说明这一点：Andrew，

blocks.en_text: a 9-year-old boy who attacked a little girl on the baseball field
blocks.zh_text: 一个9岁的男孩，在棒球场上攻击了一个小女孩

blocks.en_text: for no particular reason,
blocks.zh_text: 没有什么特别的原因，

blocks.en_text: and at the time, was drawing pictures of himself
blocks.zh_text: 而且当时，他正在画自己的画

blocks.en_text: hanging from a tree and shooting other children.
blocks.zh_text: 画的是自己吊在树上，朝其他孩子开枪。

blocks.en_text: Andrew was Columbine, Aurora,
blocks.zh_text: Andrew就是Columbine、Aurora，

blocks.en_text: and Sandy Hook waiting to happen.
blocks.zh_text: 和Sandy Hook事件的潜在重演。

blocks.en_text: Most psychiatrists would have medicated Andrew,
blocks.zh_text: 大多数精神科医生会给Andrew用药，

blocks.en_text: as they did Eric Harris and the other mass shooters
blocks.zh_text: 就像他们对Eric Harris和其他大规模枪击者所做的那样

blocks.en_text: before they committed their awful crimes,
blocks.zh_text: 在他们犯下可怕的罪行之前，

blocks.en_text: but SPECT imaging taught me that I had to look at his brain
blocks.zh_text: 但SPECT成像教会我，我必须看看他的大脑

blocks.en_text: and not throw darts in the dark at him to understand what he needed.
blocks.zh_text: 而不是在黑暗中对他乱扔飞镖，来理解他需要什么。

blocks.en_text: His SPECT scan showed a cyst, the size of a golf ball,
blocks.zh_text: 他的SPECT扫描显示了一个囊肿，高尔夫球大小，

blocks.en_text: occupying the space of his left temple lobe.
blocks.zh_text: 占据了他左侧颞叶的空间。

blocks.en_text: No amount of medication or therapy would have helped Andrew.
blocks.zh_text: 再多的药物或治疗都不会对Andrew有帮助。

blocks.en_text: When the cyst was removed,
blocks.zh_text: 当囊肿被切除后，

blocks.en_text: his behavior completely went back to normal,
blocks.zh_text: 他的行为完全恢复了正常，

blocks.en_text: and he became the sweet, loving boy he always wanted to be.
blocks.zh_text: 他变成了他一直想成为的那个甜美、有爱心的男孩。

blocks.en_text: Now 18 years later, Andrew, who is my nephew,
blocks.zh_text: 18年后的今天，Andrew，也就是我的侄子，

blocks.en_text: owns his own home, is employed and pays taxes.
blocks.zh_text: 拥有自己的房子，有工作，还纳税。

blocks.en_text: Because someone bothered to look at his brain,
blocks.zh_text: 因为有人费心去看了他的大脑，

blocks.en_text: he has been a better son,
blocks.zh_text: 他成了一个更好的儿子，

blocks.en_text: and will be a better husband, father, and grandfather.
blocks.zh_text: 将来也会成为更好的丈夫、父亲和祖父。

blocks.en_text: When you have the privilege of changing someone's brain,
blocks.zh_text: 当你有幸改变某人的大脑时，

blocks.en_text: you not only change his or her life
blocks.zh_text: 你不仅改变了他或她的生活

blocks.en_text: but you have the opportunity to change generations to come.
blocks.zh_text: 你还有机会改变未来的几代人。

blocks.en_text: I'm Dr. Daniel Amen. Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 我是Daniel Amen医生。谢谢。
